title: Mega-Method (The Monster Function)
pattern: A monolithic, extremely long function executing several distinct phases of a business process (parsing, auditing, business math, network output) sequentially within a single execution block.
why_bad: Violates the Single Responsibility Principle and local reasoning. Local variables from separate phases bleed into each other, inviting accidental state corruption. It is impossible to test or mock any individual segment (like the discount logic) without triggering all other phases (like database writes or SMTP network calls).
detection: Measure functions containing hundreds of lines executing structurally distinct responsibilities (indicated by large, contiguous blocks separated by comment headers such as "// Parse", "// Write to DB", "// Send Email").
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level parser-combinators or assembly generators where a flat, linear execution sequence is highly optimized and necessary.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 7, "High-Quality Routines"; *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Long Method" (p. 64); *Michael C. Feathers - Working Effectively with Legacy Code (2004)*, Chapter 22, "I Need to Change a Monster Method".
